item.title: Sustainable Strategic Knowledge Management in the Era of AI
item.content:encoded:
Krishna Venkitachalam, Ajman University

Nina Helander, Tampere University

Organizations face increasing volatility and complexity, creating significant knowledge gaps. Sustainable strategic knowledge management has become essential for leveraging intellectual assets—employees' knowledge, skills, and expertise—to achieve financial, social, and environmental objectives.

Artificial intelligence presents opportunities and challenges for knowledge management. AI can enhance decision-making through human-AI synergy and optimize resource use, but organizations must manage AI-generated knowledge responsibly, addressing knowledge overload, duplication, and inefficient transfer. This requires balancing AI capabilities with human expertise while maintaining ethical standards.

This special issue seeks contributions on implementing sustainable strategic knowledge management in AI-enabled environments, including knowledge codification and personalization strategies, managing explicit and tacit knowledge, addressing digital overload, and developing ethical frameworks for AI-integrated knowledge systems.

Appel publié par Journal of strategy and management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Knowledge management processes and sustainability
  • Human-AI synergy and intelligent knowledge systems
  • Strategic knowledge management in digital landscapes
  • Ethical and responsible AI implementation
  • Tacit and explicit knowledge management
  • Knowledge codification and personalization approaches
  • AI-driven knowledge overload and management
  • Sustainable organizational knowledge strategies
  • Knowledge loss prevention and resource optimization
  • AI impact on organizational knowledge processes
